summary: "Mijbil the Otter" by Gavin Maxwell is a delightful travelogue and pet narrative that details the author's fascinating experience of owning and journeying with an intelligent, playful otter named Mijbil. Following the death of his pet dog, Maxwell decides to keep an otter instead and travels to the Tigris marshes in Iraq, where his friend presents him with an otter cub wrapped in a sack. Christened "Mijbil," the creature initially appears aloof but quickly transforms into a hyperactive companion with an obsessive love for running water, learning to open the bathroom tap on his own and plunging into the tub with absolute joy. The real challenge arises when Maxwell must transport Mijbil from Basra to London via Paris, as British airlines do not allow animals on board. Per airline regulations, the narrator must secure Mijbil inside a small cardboard box. However, just  before leaving for the airport, the mischievous otter tears the box's inner lining, cutting himself and causing blood to trickle out, forcing a frantic rush to the flight. On board the aircraft, the situation descends into pure chaos when Mijbil breaks free from his box, disappears under the seats, and causes a woman to scream in panic thinking he is a rat. Order is restored when the sympathetic flight attendant assists Maxwell, allowing Mijbil to return calmly to the author's lap. Settling into their flat in London, Mijbil quickly adapts to city life by inventing his own unique games, such as balancing a ping-pong ball on the sloping lid of a suitcase and bouncing it across the room. He also accompanies the author on daily walks, developing a playful routine of galloping along a low wall outside a primary school, much to the distraction of the students. The chapter concludes with the amusing reactions of Londoners, who are completely unfamiliar with otters and constantly misidentify Mijbil as a baby seal, a squirrel, a walrus, a beaver, or even a miniature brontosaurus, highlighting the unique and unpredictable joy of bringing a piece of the wild into the civilized world.

qa.q: What does Maxwell say about otters?
qa.a: ​ Maxwell says that otters are playful and intelligent animals. They are easily tamed and can form a close bond with human beings. He had always been interested in keeping an otter as a pet.

qa.q: Why did Maxwell decide to keep an otter as a pet?
qa.a: ​ Maxwell wanted an otter as a pet because he was fascinated by these animals. He had heard about otters and wanted to experience their playful and friendly nature himself.

qa.q: What did Mijbil do when Maxwell first brought him home?
qa.a: ​ When Mijbil first came home, he was shy and quiet. Gradually, he became comfortable with Maxwell and began exploring the house. Soon he became playful and developed a close relationship with his owner.
​ Mijbil loved playing with water and objects around the house. He played with marbles, a rubber ball and other small objects. He also enjoyed playing in water and created his own games.

qa.q: What special qualities did Mijbil possess?
qa.a: ​ Mijbil was intelligent, playful, curious and affectionate. He loved water and enjoyed inventing games with different objects. He was also very active and quickly became attached to Maxwell.

qa.q: Why did Maxwell have to take Mijbil to London?
qa.a: ​ Maxwell had to return to London after his stay in Iraq, so he decided to take Mijbil with him. Since otters were not allowed in the aircraft cabin, he had to make special arrangements for the journey.

qa.q: What happened when Mijbil was placed in the box before the flight?
qa.a: ​ Mijbil became frightened and struggled inside the box. He damaged the box and escaped before the journey. Maxwell was worried because Mijbil disappeared, but he eventually found him and managed to take him to the airport.

qa.q: Why did the passengers in the aircraft think Mijbil was a strange creature?
qa.a: ​ The passengers had never seen an otter before. They were curious about Mijbil and tried to identify him. One passenger even thought he was a strange type of squirrel. Their reactions show how unusual an otter was to them.
